candidates.story: A2ABreak systematic security analysis of the A2A protocol
candidates.reason: The cs.CR RSS event is exact and 22 hours 12 minutes 35.5 seconds old at run start. The paper, released artifacts and current versioned specification support a consequential and bounded deployment decision. No existing article, source ledger or newsroom story covers A2ABreak, arXiv 2609.10871 or A2A context ownership.

candidates.story: MCP Registry usability paper retained from the prior run
candidates.reason: Its previously verified event time was 48 hours 38 minutes 42.5 seconds old at this run's start, outside the hard 48-hour publication window. A retained draft cannot override freshness.

The report is fresh by date, but the accessible primary material does not establish an unambiguous exact main-event time and timezone. Its operational-security theme also overlaps recent Index Us coverage more closely than the selected protocol-invariant analysis.
The paper is fresh but substantially overlaps the held MCP Registry story. A2ABreak provides a more distinct reader decision with current specification evidence and released formal artifacts.
The study changes model, harness, autonomy and memory together, so an automatic long-form article could not attribute the result cleanly enough for a practical deployment recommendation.

candidates.story: Salesforce AI harness and job-ready agents announcement
candidates.reason: Available evidence is announcement-led and too thin for a defensible independent long-form claim about job readiness or harness performance.

The post describes substantive infrastructure work but is not the strongest current AI deployment decision. The selected A2A analysis has a fresher exact event, primary artifacts and a clearer cross-organisation security consequence.

decision.reason: A2ABreak is an exact-timestamped, priority-window and non-duplicate protocol-security development. The paper and artifacts identify testable missing invariants, while the current A2A specification supplies important countervailing evidence that authorisation is already mandatory. A2ASecBench adds independent implementation-oriented context without being presented as confirmation.

claims.text: The arXiv cs.CR RSS feed announced A2ABreak at exactly 2026-09-11T04:00:00Z.
claims.sourceLocator: s1 item pubDate and guid

claims.text: The public A2ABreak text reviewed here is arXiv v1, submitted at 2026-09-09T22:18:36Z.
claims.sourceLocator: s2 header and arXiv submission history

claims.text: A2ABreak uses an LLM-assisted specification pipeline and reports 929 verified statements, a 37-state/76-transition A2A finite-state machine and 11 final findings under a full-compliance adversary.
claims.sourceLocator: s2 abstract, Sections III-IV, Section VI and Table III; s3 README and final_verified.json

claims.text: The paper does not verify specific agent implementations or production deployments and does not establish that every A2A implementation is vulnerable.
claims.sourceLocator: s2 Section III-A scope; the universal implementation conclusion is explicitly withheld in the final article

claims.text: At commit f63dbb482719, A2A section 13.1 requires authorization checks on every protocol-operation request and caller-scoped access boundaries, with specific checks for task listing, retrieval, cancellation, subscription and push-notification configuration.
claims.sourceLocator: s5 Section 13.1 Data Access and Authorization Scoping

claims.text: The current A2A specification defines contextId as an optional grouping value, permits context-only creation of a new task in an existing context, and allows an agent to maintain state or LLM context across interactions sharing that identifier.
claims.sourceLocator: s5 Sections 3.4.1 and 3.4.3; s8 Task and Message fields

claims.text: The protocol data model does not define a context owner, creator or context access token, while each agent defines its own authorization model.
claims.sourceLocator: s5 Section 13.1 Implementation Requirements; s8 Task and Message context_id fields; absence checked across the pinned specification and data model

claims.text: A2ABreak's context finding is best read as a missing required context-admission relationship within the general authorization model, not as evidence that A2A lacks authorization or that safe implementations cannot reject cross-boundary admission.
claims.sourceLocator: Premises: s2 Section VI context finding; s4 GapSurvivesSection131 model description; s5 Section 13.1 and context semantics. Boundary: Index Us reconciliation of the paper and current spec, not a maintainer ruling.

claims.text: The A2A specification history includes a 30 July 2026 clarification of in-task authorization scope and further documentation changes through the pinned 28 August commit.
claims.sourceLocator: s6 commits 6550d344b39c and f63dbb482719

claims.text: The visible A2ABreak article refers to A2A v1.0 and a live specification URL but does not identify an immutable specification commit, so this article pins the comparison to f63dbb482719.
claims.sourceLocator: s2 Sections II-A and references; no commit identifier in visible article; s5 immutable commit used for current comparison

claims.text: The paper's cross-client context scenario assumes an authenticated caller knows another contextId and the server uses shared context state; the new task can then influence or receive a response informed by that state without directly retrieving the victim's task.
claims.sourceLocator: s2 Section VI finding 3; s3 final_verified.json context finding

claims.text: The released bounded Alloy context model records a counterexample while its encoded section 13.1 task rule holds and records no counterexample for its mitigation check after a context-owner relation is added.
claims.sourceLocator: s4 README What each model proves and results/finding3/context_receipt.json commands GapSurvivesSection131 and Mitigated

claims.text: Binding contexts to explicit principals, tenants, projects or authorized sets and checking admission before state access is a practical implementation control; opaque identifiers alone are not authorization.
claims.sourceLocator: Premises: context semantics, section 13.1 agent-defined authorization models, and author model's ownership mitigation. Boundary: Index Us implementation recommendation, not protocol requirement or tested result.

claims.text: A2A permits chains of tasks in AUTH_REQUIRED, warns that in-band credentials can be exposed to agents along the chain, recommends binding credentials to the originating agent, and leaves authorization scope and representation to implementations, issuers or extensions.
claims.sourceLocator: s5 Sections 7.6.2, 7.6.3 and 7.6.4

claims.text: A2ABreak argues that the protocol lacks a standard origin and delegation-lineage object, and its TLA+ artifacts treat origin propagation and credential audience-binding as separate protections.
claims.sourceLocator: s2 Section VI finding 9; s4 README Multi-Hop Identity Loss and TLA configurations

claims.text: A multi-hop authorization deployment should retain auditable origin, chain and requested scope and issue credentials for narrow audiences and operations.
claims.sourceLocator: Premises: s5 chain exposure and credential-binding guidance; s4 provenance and binding model. Boundary: Index Us deployment recommendation, not current A2A guarantee.

claims.text: AgentSkill contains descriptive capability fields, while AgentCard supports JWS signatures; with a trusted verification key, a card signature can authenticate an assertion's publisher and integrity but does not demonstrate capability truth or quality.
claims.sourceLocator: Premises: s8 AgentSkill, AgentCard and AgentCardSignature; s5 Agent Card sections; s4 README Unattested Skill Claims. Boundary: cryptographic distinction and deployment interpretation, not a performance test.

claims.text: The released bounded Alloy skill model records a counterexample for a signed but false capability assertion and records no counterexample for its signed-attestation restoration check within the tested scope.
claims.sourceLocator: s4 README and results/finding1/skill_receipt.json commands SignedCapabilityHonored and SignedAttestationRestores

claims.text: Across five A2ABreak analysis runs, 17 unique candidates were found, 16 passed the authors' adversarial stage, and expert manual review removed one duplicate and four false positives, producing 11 final findings with reported precision 73.3 per cent and F1 84.6 per cent.
claims.sourceLocator: s2 Section V RQ2, lines describing candidate and expert-review counts

claims.text: For FSM extraction validation the authors used TCP and PSMBench as a proxy, recovering 11 of 11 states and 19 of 20 transitions while extracting 25 transitions in total, because no equivalent A2A ground truth exists.
claims.sourceLocator: s2 Section V RQ2 and Table I; s3 PSM_Benchmark artifacts

claims.text: The released repository contains the curated 11-finding file and formal artifacts for only three detailed findings: context ownership, skill attestation and multi-hop identity loss.
claims.sourceLocator: s3 repository layout and outputs/final_verified.json; s4 README findings table

claims.text: The released bounded models can demonstrate counterexamples and mitigation properties under their encoded assumptions, but they do not measure exploit prevalence, implementation quality or unmodelled production behaviour.
claims.sourceLocator: Premises: s2 scope and future simulation work; s4 bounded Alloy and TLA+ model descriptions. Boundary: formal-method interpretation explicitly stated in the article.

claims.text: The accepted ICLR 2026 A2ASecBench work defines six A2A attack families, pairs adversarial and benign evaluation, and evaluates official A2A demonstration systems across travel, healthcare and finance.
claims.sourceLocator: s7 venue line and abstract

claims.text: A2ASecBench is independent context for implementation-oriented security and utility testing, but it does not confirm A2ABreak's 11 specification findings.
claims.sourceLocator: Premises: the papers examine different methods, attack families and evidence objects. Boundary: explicit non-confirmation statement in final article.

claims.text: A deployment evaluation should convert context admission, delegation lineage, capability assurance and lifecycle risks into acceptance tests and run matched benign tasks to measure compatibility costs.
claims.sourceLocator: Premises: paper findings, current mandatory controls and A2ASecBench joint safety-utility method. Boundary: Index Us practical evaluation framework, not a measured result.
